figures.evidence: Monostable.md:361-367 at 23c82ca places the gated device between the RP2350's output pins and the output connector. F13 (Research.md:541) names the 20 output ports and the UART socket. V71 (Research.md:631) gives EX Bus and SRXL2 telemetry toward the receiver only.

The RUN and brownout part stands. Section 9.3 lists brownout, RUN, SW-DP CDBGRSTREQ and RP-AP rescue reset as returning pads to reset state (output hi-Z, pulled low). Table 1436 gives a pull-down of 36 to 113 kOhm. The watchdog part is wrong. It rests on the isolation latches of section 9.7, but those hold a pad only while its ISO bit is set. The SDK clears ISO in gpio_set_function (section 9.3 IMPORTANT note). Section 9.7 also says ISO bits are not reset by a PADS block reset, and that 'resetting the PADS register block returns non-isolated pads to their reset state'. The datasheet's own listing of the SDK's _watchdog_enable (section 12.9.6.1, lines 52-53) sets PSM_WDSEL to every stage except ROSC and XOSC. That includes the RESETS stage (PSM WDSEL bit 4, Table 532). The RESETS reset value holds PADS_BANK0 and IO_BANK0 in reset (bits 9 and 6 = 0x1). So after a watchdog reset under the SDK's configuration, the gated lines return to pulled-low. The watchdog level depends on the firmware's PSM_WDSEL and RESETS_WDSEL settings; the isolation latches do not set it.

figures.figure: P2 report: connector level through a watchdog reset
figures.evidence: The quoted list in section 9.3 is right. The conclusion does not follow. The isolation latches of section 9.7 hold a pad only while its ISO bit is set, and the SDK clears ISO in gpio_set_function. Section 9.7 says a PADS block reset does not reset the ISO bits and returns non-isolated pads to their reset state. The SDK's _watchdog_enable, listed in section 12.9.6.1, sets PSM_WDSEL to every stage except ROSC and XOSC, which includes RESETS (Table 532 bit 4). The RESETS reset value holds PADS_BANK0 and IO_BANK0 in reset. So under that configuration the gated lines return to hi-Z and pulled-low. The line stays high only if firmware leaves those stages out of PSM_WDSEL and RESETS_WDSEL. That is a firmware configuration for P5 and R1, not an effect of the isolation latches.

figures.figure: P2 report: drive on the switch path
figures.evidence: Table 1436 at IOVDD 3.3 V gives VOH >= 2.62 V and VOL <= 0.5 V at IOH/IOL = 2, 4, 8 or 12 mA 'depending on setting'. With the 1 kOhm pull-up, 300 Ohm and the pull-downs, the pad sinks about 2.3 mA while low. That exceeds the 2 mA setting, so a setting of 4 mA or higher is needed.

The TMUX1511, SN74CB3Q3125 and SN74LVC126A readings are right. TMUX1511 (SCDS390B) gives IPOFF +/-2 uA to 3.6 V on S/D only, and SEL IIH/IIL only with VDD powered; section 7.3.5 is fail-safe logic. SN74CB3Q3125 (SCDS143E, revised September 2026) gives Ioff with VO 0 to 5.5 V and VI = 0, and control IIN only at VCC 3.6 V. SN74LVC126A (SCAS339U) states no Ioff. The SN74LVC8T245 and TXU0104 readings are not right. Their tables list Ioff under 'A or B port', but the text assigns that limit to every pin. SCES584D (revised May 2026) section 7.3.2: 'The maximum leakage into or out of any input or output pin on the device is specified by Ioff' (+/-2 uA). SCES937B section 7.3.4 says the same, and section 7.3 says Ioff protection covers 'an input or output while the device is powered down'. So each datasheet does state a limit for OE at supply 0 V, by reference, and the 'no figure for the enable input' drops of those two parts need a ruling.

SCDS038N (revised July 2026) section 5.5 tabulates ron only at VI 0 V (64 and 24 mA) and VI 2.4 V (15 mA: 10 Ohm typical, 15 Ohm maximum at VCC 3 V). Features and section 7.3 state 'Rail-to-rail switching on data I/O'.

The 0.76 V (3.3 x 300/1300) puts the RP2354B pad at 0 V. Table 1436 bounds the pad low only at VOL <= 0.5 V at the set IOL. The switch adds up to 7 Ohm (SCDS038N 5.5), and the 10 kOhm and servo 3 kOhm pull-downs share the node. With the pad at its datasheet limit of 0.5 V, the low at the servo is about 1.05 V. With the pad at 0 V it is 0.69 V. The datasheet-bounded low is therefore up to about 1.05 V, not 0.76 V. The servo's input-low threshold is still not stated.
